sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: An annual or biennial herb, usually low-growing but reaching about 80 cm. Its leaves are finely divided; flower heads 1–4 cm across combine white ray florets and a yellow disc. The receptacle becomes conical and bears pale scales between the florets. Native from Macaronesia and Europe through the Mediterranean region to Iran, it has been introduced elsewhere.

sections.title: Identification and uses
sections.text: The scales on the receptacle distinguish it from the often-confused Tripleurospermum inodorum, which lacks them. No established food use was found in the sources consulted.
